chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Zuhri al-Kufi narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn Isa al-Hasani narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Bata'ini from his father from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) said:

"Indeed, the example of our Shia is like a threshing floor (meaning a large heap) containing grain. A worm afflicts it and it is purified, then another worm afflicts it and it is purified, until what remains is that which does not harm the worm. So too are our Shia: they are distinguished and purified until a small group remains, who are not harmed by the tribulation."

key_terms.أَنْدَرُ: A large heap or threshing floor (specifically of grain)
key_terms.عِصَابَةٌ: A small, distinct group or band

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used by Imam al-Baqir to describe the purification of the Shia during times of tribulation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of grain infested by worms to illustrate the gradual purification of the Shia through successive trials, where the weak are eliminated until a steadfast remnant remains immune to tribulation. This hadith, found in al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, provides crucial context for the era of the Minor and Major Disappearance, emphasizing that internal differentiation and external pressures serve as a divine mechanism to preserve the core of true belief. It underscores the Shia theological view that fitnah is not merely a test of endurance but a process of selective preservation for the final victorious group.
